Pages hold block markup; <!-- wp:pattern {"slug":"..."} /--> is expanded into the pattern's blocks on import. "{{theme}}" stands for the theme folder URL. "screens" lists the URL of each catalogue page. "productCategories", "productTags" and "products" are imported by inc/woo-import.php, only while WooCommerce is active; each product's "Edition" and "Size (cm)" attributes are the single source of the small edition line (e.g. edition of 30 · 45 cm) printed above its price. The shop address, hours, telephone and email, and the edition terms, are not in this file: they live in synced patterns (inc/shared-info.php, inc/info/*.html).

site.title: Aoi Hanga
site.tagline: Woodblock prints cut, inked and pressed by hand by the river.

categories.name: Studio notes
categories.description: The studio, the river and the paper shop downstairs.

posts.title: Mixing spring green
posts.excerpt: Moegi is the green of new leaves. It takes three pigments and a morning to match the last batch.
posts.content:
Moegi is the green of new leaves, and it is the colour we mix most. It takes three pigments, rice paste and a morning to match the last batch by eye.

Three pigments

A yellow, an indigo and a little sumi to quieten it. Too much indigo and it turns to pine; too little and it looks like lemon peel.

We test every batch on a scrap sheet pinned by the window, and only start the edition when it matches the proof.

posts.title: A heron in thirty sheets
posts.excerpt: The new heron took eleven days to cut and four days to press. Thirty sheets, numbered in pencil.
posts.content:
The new heron took eleven days to cut and four days to press. The reeds are one block, the bird another, the water a third.

Why thirty

After thirty sheets the finest lines start to soften. We stop there, sign each one and keep the block for mending.

posts.title: The paper shop downstairs
posts.excerpt: Our paper comes up the stairs one sheet at a time from the shop below.
posts.content:
Our paper comes up the stairs one sheet at a time from the shop below. Kozo washi, sized with a thin glue so the ink sits on top.

Damp, not wet

Sheets are dampened the night before and stacked between boards so they are soft enough to take the ink.

posts.title: Pine Ridge in the mist
posts.excerpt: Pine Ridge is printed in five greys and one green, from the hills you see behind the river.
posts.content:
Pine Ridge is printed in five greys and one green. The hills are the ones you see behind the river on a wet morning.

Bokashi

The mist is a gradation wiped onto the block with a damp cloth before each pass: no two sheets are quite the same.
